title: Reproducible protocol for the extraction and semi-automated quantification of macroscopic charcoal from soil
author: Javier Ruiz-Pérez

steps.title: Prepare Soil Samples
steps.instruction: Oven-dry soil samples to a constant weight at 40 ºC. Weigh 20 g of each dry soil sample into labeled ≥200 mL beakers.

substeps.instruction: Dry samples at 40 ºC (do not exceed this temperature to prevent clay hardening and charcoal breakage) until weight is constant.
Tare beakers and record the weight of the 20 g soil sample.
If using tools (e.g., spoons) for transfer, clean them with 99% isopropyl alcohol between samples to prevent cross-contamination.
Adjust sample mass or beaker size proportionately if the expected charcoal content differs from the standard 20 g.

steps.title: Disperse and Digest Soils
steps.instruction: Add a chemical solution to the soil samples and shake to disperse the soil and digest organic matter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 1:1 mixture of 50 mL of 5% sodium hexametaphosphate (Na6P6O18) and 50 mL of 10% hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) to create a solution of 2.5% sodium hexametaphosphate and 5% hydrogen peroxide.
Add 100 mL of this solution to each 20 g soil sample (maintain a ratio of 5 mL solution per 1 g or cm³ of dry sample).
For organic-rich samples, add the solution in small quantities and monitor for vigorous oxidation reactions.
Place beakers in an orbital shaker at 250-300 RPM for 24 hours (reduce speed for fragile fragments or substitute with gentle manual shaking).
Note: Avoid hydrogen peroxide or use milder concentrations if recovering charcoal produced at 250-400 ºC.

steps.title: Sieve Samples
steps.instruction: Separate macroscopic charcoal from the soil matrix using a mesh sieve.

substeps.instruction: Place a 500-micron mesh sieve over a container or sink.
Gently pour the soil/solution mixture from the beaker into the sieve using a wash bottle with purified water.
Rinse the sample with purified water (wash bottle or faucet) until only particles ≥500 microns remain and charcoal fragments are clean.
Use different or nested mesh sizes if recovering charcoal of sizes other than ≥500 microns.

steps.title: Collect and Store Charcoal
steps.instruction: Isolate charcoal fragments, remove moisture, and store for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Label and weigh sample containers (e.g., vials).

Collect charcoal fragments from the sieve using tweezers and transfer to containers, discarding non-charcoal material. For fragile fragments or smaller mesh sizes, use a wash bottle and Chattaway spatula for transfer.
Oven-dry the open containers at 40 ºC to remove moisture (do not exceed 40 ºC).
Visually inspect fragments (naked eye or magnification) to remove any remaining non-charcoal bodies.
Weigh the containers with extracted charcoal and record the weight.
Close lids and store in a dry environment.

steps.title: Acquire Images of Charcoal
steps.instruction: Photograph the extracted charcoal fragments using a stereo microscope.

substeps.instruction: Clean a Petri dish (preferably gridded) with 99% isopropyl alcohol and allow it to evaporate.
Transfer charcoal to the Petri dish using tweezers, a Chattaway spatula, or purified water in small amounts to avoid overlapping fragments.
Capture images using a light stereo microscope with a digital camera at 10-15x magnification (for fragments ≥500 µm).
Ensure consistent settings (resolution, exposure, white balance) across all images.
Use transmitted light for pure charcoal extracts, or reflected/combined light if sand grains are present.
Acquire at least one image with a reference scale bar for calibration.
Save images in a dedicated folder and create a separate folder for ImageJ results.

steps.title: Quantify Charcoal using ImageJ
steps.instruction: Use ImageJ and the provided macro to automatically count and measure charcoal fragments.

substeps.instruction: Download ImageJ and save the provided macro code as a .txt file.
Run the macro via Plugins -> Macros -> Run... and enter the following in the parameters window:
Input and output folders for images and results.

Scale parameters: Scale unit, known distance in original unit, and equivalent pixels (determined by opening a scale bar image, using the Straight Line tool with Shift, and selecting Analyze -> Set Scale).
Thresholding method: Select 'Manual' (and enter min/max pixel values 0-255) or an 'Automatic' method.
Size range of fragments to be counted (e.g., 500 to Infinity).
Toggle Watershed segmentation (to separate contacting fragments) and Hole filling.
Select outline image format (JPEG or TIFF).
The macro will export a parameters CSV, a measurement CSV (area, length, width), and outline images.
